items.label: BOOT
items.why: The other disk's boot: a cracker's obfuscated start that jumps through ($01FF) into the file 2 at $C240, which loads LO and HI with the KERNAL

items.label: {14}BLOCKS FREE.{00}{00}{00}
items.why: The cracker's second stage (the same bytes as the files 2 and PROT!), under a directory entry that reads BLOCKS FREE.

items.label: HELLO
items.why: A cracker's file of 772 bytes for $888E holding encoded text; the game never names it. Not studied further

items.label: LO
items.why: The other build of the whole program, packed (47,103 bytes from $0801): the same game assembled again with 16 bytes added at $0800, which the other disk's boot loads in place of the build analysed here

items.label: HI
items.why: The rest of the other build (8,960 bytes, a mover at its start, then the tables and code from $DD1F up to the top of memory, the same as this build's from $F51B on)

items.label: BOND
items.why: The analysed disk's only file: a fast loader in the stack page that starts code in the drive with M-E and reads the rest of the disk, outside the directory, two bits at a time; it calls $3F00 to move $4000-$5BFF under the I/O area and then the Trilogic Expert unpacker at $0800 (orientation.md)
